rationale:
No stall signal is showing, so nothing forced my hand; the ladder was chosen from what the picture is missing. Rung 4b is discharged — the last two passes both sat there and #186/#189 finally moved the census's shape, so mapFlat is quiet — and the last rung 5 was #164, twenty-seven iterations ago. This batch is rung 5: change the observer.

I shot the town at seed 42, t 175, and then went and counted, because the watch note forbids an impression standing in for a number. The bottom of every frame at every framing is the sill: sillTop() = H - max(26, H*0.075), so it is the bottom 7.5% of the picture, and the objects on it are drawn at sillU() scale, which makes them the largest figures in the frame against 12 px people. drawSill() puts three things there — two pots of geraniums and a forgotten cup — and its only input from the world is `daylight`. Not season(), not warmth, not snowCover, not wetF, not raining, not windF, not one fact about the town it looks at. It is the same picture in February and July, in a gale and in snow. This is not the 'that surface looks flat' brief the watch note kills on sight: the sill's texture measures sd/mean 0.671, the highest in the table, and it is beautifully drawn. The claim is that the piece's own framing device is the one thing in it that the year does not pass through, and that the sill domain has had zero new elements in 190 iterations. b191 is 80 minutes with an explicit 150-300 line licence, first in the queue.

The other four each carry the number they rest on. b192 found the second unpriced thing this pass: riverRun() has said since #145 that the channel runs x1.45 in January and x0.55 in July, has fifteen consumers, and every one of them is colour, speed, streak count or the mill — the WATERLINE has never moved, and it is the last big seasonal surface that does not. b193 is c277 with #184's supply measurement in the brief. b194 is the plaza, which after 190 iterations still has no day of its own while the lane, the far bank and the cross street each have one. b195 is c278: a probe that threw on every run for seven iterations, in a tree of 303 files nothing executes.

queue.brief: THE BET — take the swing; a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. Grep drawSill() (~line 12131) before anything else and confirm the premise for yourself: it is ~90 lines, it draws three objects — two geranium pots and a forgotten cup, from sillPots() — and its ONLY input from the world is `daylight`, via `warm = 0.10 + 0.55 * daylight` and `lit`. Nothing in it reads season(), warmth, growSeason(), snowCover, wetF, raining, windF, chillF or any town state. Yet it is the bottom 7.5% of every frame at every framing (sillTop() = H - max(26, H * 0.075)), it is drawn at sillU() scale so its objects are the largest figures in the picture, and it is the one place in the world the observer is nominally standing. Make the ledge a place the year and the weather pass through: geraniums that come on and die back, rain that beads on the glass and darkens the stone, a rim of snow or frost on the outer nosing in winter, the cup that comes and goes. What exactly it holds is yours to choose — the requirement is that a February evening and a July morning are two different pictures at the bottom of the frame, and that the difference is legible at the shipping size. The sill domain has had ZERO new elements in 190 iterations; this is the piece's framing device and it has never changed.
queue.successLooksLike: Two shots at one seed, size and hour — one in February, one in July — and the bottom of the frame is two different pictures, quoted as diff MASS against a same-code control that reads 0. Plus: the ground cache's repaint rate is still at or under #180's 75.14/day (probes/ground-rebuilds.mjs exists), and whatever you put on the ledge ANSWERS THE POINTER — c282, folded in here: the pots and the cup have never had a name.
queue.avoid: drawSill is baked INTO the ground cache, from inside drawOurSide. Anything that must be true per frame is a live overlay drawn after, not a new reason to rebuild the cache — #180 cut the repaint rate 110.78 -> 75.14/day and this must not push it back; measure it, do not assume it. Nothing here may draw from R(): the sill is a CANVAS-EXTENT population and the draws a frame spends are a fact about the WINDOW, so use hash(). And do NOT crowd it — the sill is the frame, and the change through the year is the content, not the number of objects. If you end with more silhouettes than you started with and they do not each earn their place, you have made a shelf, not a sill.

queue.brief: riverRun() = 1 + RIVER_SWING * greyF() has said since #145 that the channel runs x1.45 in January and x0.55 in July. It has FIFTEEN call sites and every one of them is colour, drift speed, streak count, streak length, millSpin, the fountain, or the deep-channel gradient in groundBase. Not one moves the WATERLINE: RIVER_X0 114..RIVER_X1 127 is a build-time constant, and the census's `water` has read 8784 (976 cells x 9 samples) for forty iterations. So the river is the last big surface in the town where the season changes how it LOOKS and not where it IS. Give it a level at the margin: high water in winter laps up over the reed shallows and toward the towpath, a low late summer uncovers a strip of wet stone and reed roots at the edge. Build it on the machinery #181 already has — buildIce/stepIce enumerate the margin as an L1 distance transform out from every cell the channel is NOT, and riverMid(x) already says where the current is too fast for anything to happen.
queue.successLooksLike: A probe on the pattern of probes/river-ice.mjs, 6 seeds x a year, reporting the wetted margin as a CURVE with a winter maximum and a late-summer minimum — not a switch; quote the most cells that cross a drawn bucket in one tick, as #181 did (it was 13). The bank strip is uncovered on N days and exactly 0 on the rest. Boats, ducks, swans, the mirror and the ice are all still correct at BOTH extremes, and the winter census row moves.
queue.avoid: NEITHER census block can see the low-water end. The three summer ages all sit at warmth 0.6929 by design (#14) and #187's winter block is pinned at warp 1220, so expect the summer nine UNCHANGED and say so in the brief's own words rather than promising a delta you cannot get — that trap cost #181 a whole paragraph. Prove the summer end with your own probe. A level that flips tiles is a grid change: re-pin with census.mjs --save-baseline and check `developed` and `green` did not absorb what `water` lost. And keep it a MARGIN — do not narrow the navigable channel or the punts, the barge and the rowboat all need re-pricing.

queue.brief: c277, promoted. MK_NEED = [0, 4, 13] (line ~3369) is read in exactly one place — mkTrades(i), line ~3461 — and it decides how many of the three market stalls open. #184 measured the supply it is set against and the numbers are in the ledger: the store hands the market a MEDIAN 53.1 units against MK_CAP 18 over 51 markets, three stalls are open on 86% of them, and mkTotal is never 0 (minimum 0.7). The 4 and the 13 are therefore dead constants and 'a thin February market' is unreachable. Re-measure that distribution yourself first — #184's numbers are eight iterations old and the crate work has since drawn off the top of it — then set the thresholds against the supply the market ACTUALLY sees across a year, so a lean market opens two pitches and a fat one three, and the lane in late winter is visibly a smaller market than the lane in September.
queue.successLooksLike: A histogram of mkTotal per market, 6 seeds x a year, with the open-stall count by season beside it; stalls-open is no longer 3 on 86% of markets, and the season it thins in is the season the allotments are bare. drawMarketOver's crate curve (0.67 spring / 1.87 winter / 5.33 summer / 11.44 autumn, #184) re-measured, since it is cut from the same mkUnits and will move with this.
queue.avoid: Do not add a fourth stall — #184 already found the CROWD is the bound, not the shelf (0.72 browsers a market, median 0). Do not read a ratio: identical numbers at two settings is a DEAD constant and the supply was always the cap, so sweep the AXIS — the season — and not the constant, and pool six seeds. If the honest answer turns out to be that MK_NEED should be a function of the season rather than a fixed ladder, say so and build that; the deliverable is a market whose size tracks the year, not three numbers.

queue.brief: The town's calendar, in full: a MARKET in the lane every 4th day (isMarketDay), a CONCERT on the far-bank bandstand in summer (isBandDay, bandChance = clamp((warmth - 0.42) / 0.4, 0, 1) * 0.86), a BONFIRE on the cross street 1.79 times a year (#185 counted it), and a CART down the cross street on 80% of mornings (CART_P 0.8). Grep for a plaza equivalent: there is none. The plaza is the town's civic room — a fountain that reads the year, the wind and the frost, a roundel, PLAZA_PITS, six benches, six FOUNT_STANDS, a quay rail, five bollards, a barge berth and a fourteen-place door that has refused 0 of 92 offers EVER (#183) — and in 190 iterations nothing has ever brought the town TO it. Give the plaza a recurring day of its own, on the calendar like the others, that pulls people out of the other quarters and fills it.
queue.successLooksLike: Presence on the plaza on the day it falls, 6 seeds x a year, is a clear multiple of an ordinary day's — measured as PRESENCE, not a per-instant crop — and you can show WHERE the people came from: count the lane and courtyard bands on the same days and show they thinned, or show the event has its own source and the neighbours are flat. On every other day the plaza is unchanged.
queue.avoid: The DOOR is not the bound — it refuses 0.0%, so capacity work here is wasted. The bound is demand, which makes this a source-and-schedule problem. A spawn BAND is a share of a budget, not a rate, so an event squeezed into an existing roll takes its crowd out of whatever sits above it in the same ladder (that is exactly what #172's allotment rung did to the plaza's own offers, 35 -> 20): if it needs its own source, give it one, and price the neighbour either way. Key the day on a salted hash(day, k) like isBandDay, never on R(). And do not make it a second market — the lane owns that.
